newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tel Aviv Exchange eases rules for foreign brokers.
newsitem.headline: Tel Aviv Exchange eases rules for foreign brokers.

text.p: The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) said on Thursday it would be amending its rules to make it easier for foreign brokerage houses to seek membership.

"It has been decided (by the board of directors) to make concession for international investment houses by modifying the definition of size and operating history, which are examined as part of the admittance procedure," the TASE said in a statement.
The TASE said the main change would be to exempt the local subsidiaries of foreign brokerage houses from the rule requiring at least two years of operations prior to application.
It said subsidiaries could apply immediately so long as the parent company was a "veteran member of a European or U.S. stock exchange" and had equity of at least $100 million.
A spokeswoman added that foreign brokerages would not be required to supply custodial services.
The TASE has 27 members, of which 13 belong to banking groups. None are affiliated with overseas firms.

The spokeswoman said the decision came in response to interest on the part of overseas brokerage houses, but she refused to identify any of them. "There is interest, not massive, but there is interest," she said.
Foreign brokers will still have to meet other requirements, which include equity of 8.2 million shekels and a customer base of least 200 accounts of at least 80,000 shekels each.
The spokeswoman said she did not know when the new rules would go into effect.
